issues.legal_issue: The eyewitness evidence was sufficiently reliable to support restoring a murder conviction on appeal from an acquittal where the evidence did not permit two reasonable views.
material_facts: Three witnesses testified that they were with the deceased when the accused attacked and killed him, and the court found their accounts reliable and their presence at the scene probable.

The witnesses’ accounts were supported by the prompt reporting of their identities as eyewitnesses, their examination soon after the occurrence, and evidence corroborating the time, place, and manner of the attack.
Two witnesses were independent of the deceased’s village, while the third was a respected local witness; the court found the reasons for rejecting their evidence unconvincing.
The investigating officer’s collection of additional circumstantial evidence to identify the body did not show that he disbelieved the eyewitnesses.
The High Court had acquitted the accused after rejecting the eyewitnesses, but the Supreme Court concluded that the evidence did not permit two views.
issues.conclusion: The acquittal was set aside and the trial court’s murder convictions were restored because the eyewitnesses were true and reliable and the evidence did not permit two views.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 of the Evidence Act, evidence must be assessed as a whole. The presence of additional circumstantial evidence does not, by itself, show that an investigating officer disbelieved eyewitness testimony. An acquittal should not stand where the reliable evidence does not permit two reasonable views. No earlier cases are cited for this holding.

rule.if: appeal_from_acquittal and eyewitnesses_reliable and not evidence_supports_two_reasonable_views

predicates.appeal_from_acquittal: The prosecution appealed a judgment acquitting persons who had been convicted at trial.
predicates.eyewitnesses_reliable: Witnesses who said they saw the crime were found credible and their presence at the scene was probable.
predicates.evidence_supports_two_reasonable_views: The evidence reasonably supports two different views of whether the accused committed the crime.
predicates.acquittal_reversed_and_conviction_restor: The acquittal is set aside and the trial conviction is restored.

issues.definition: When the prosecution appeals an acquittal, reliable eyewitness evidence and the absence of two reasonable views support setting aside the acquittal and restoring the conviction.

issues.legal_issue: A first information report’s length and detail do not, without more, justify rejecting its claimed authorship when the evidence supports its prompt preparation and consistent reporting timeline.
material_facts: The informant supplied particulars for a report that another person wrote at the scene soon after the occurrence, and the informant delivered it to the police station later that night.
Police registered the case on the report, and the investigating officer left for the scene during the night; special reports were also sent to superior officers the following morning.
The person who wrote the report gave discrepant testimony that it had instead been prepared at the police station the next morning at police direction.
The High Court doubted the informant’s authorship partly because the report was long and detailed.
issues.conclusion: The court accepted that the informant supplied the particulars and that the report was written at the scene and delivered to the police station that night; it rejected the claim that the report was prepared later at the police station.
issues.legal_principle: The headnote associates this issue with sections 144 and 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, read with section 114 of the Evidence Act. The court assessed authorship from the full evidence, including the report’s timing, the subsequent police steps, and the writer’s inconsistent testimony; length and detail alone did not establish that the report was fabricated or prepared later. No earlier cases are cited for this holding.

predicates.criminal_proceeding: The matter is a criminal prosecution in which a first information report is relied on.
predicates.report_authorship_disputed_for_length_or: A party challenges the stated informant’s authorship because the report is lengthy or contains detailed particulars.
predicates.prompt_reporting_timeline_supported_by_e: Evidence supports that the report was prepared and delivered promptly and that police acted on it soon afterward.
predicates.report_writer_testimony_inconsistent: The person who wrote the report gives inconsistent evidence about when or how it was prepared.
predicates.informant_authorship_of_report_accepted: The court accepts that the informant supplied the report’s particulars and that the report was prepared as claimed.

issues.definition: In a criminal proceeding, a challenge based on a report’s length or detail does not defeat the informant’s authorship when the prompt timeline is supported and the writer’s contrary account is inconsistent.

issues.legal_issue: A prolonged delay between a murder and the hearing of a capital appeal may justify substituting life imprisonment for death even when the murder was gruesome and cold-blooded.
material_facts: The trial court had imposed death sentences for a gruesome and cold-blooded murder.
The occurrence had taken place over a decade before the Supreme Court decided the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The court retained the convictions but altered the death sentences to life imprisonment because of the long delay before the appeal was heard.
issues.legal_principle: The headnote identifies Order XXII read with Order XLVI of the Supreme Court Rules, 1966, and Article 142(1) of the Constitution as the basis relevant to altering the sentence. The court held that the long delay justified substituting life imprisonment even though the murder was gruesome and cold-blooded. No earlier cases are cited for this holding.

predicates.capital_sentence_review: The court is reviewing a death sentence imposed for murder.
predicates.prolonged_delay_since_offence: A long period elapsed between the offence and the hearing of the appeal.
predicates.murder_was_gruesome_and_cold_blooded: The murder was found to be gruesome and cold-blooded.
predicates.death_sentence_commuted_to_life_imprison: The death sentence is replaced with a sentence of life imprisonment.

issues.definition: On review of a capital sentence, a prolonged delay since the offence supports replacing death with life imprisonment even when the murder was gruesome and cold-blooded.
